message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) belong to the order **Carnivora** (family Felidae), while zebras (Equus quagga) belong to the order **Perissodactyla** (family Equidae).  
Both orders are part of the larger clade **Laurasiatheria**, which also contains orders such as Artiodactyla (even‑toed ungulates), Chiroptera (bats), Cetartiodactyla (whales, hippos, etc.), and others.

The most recent common ancestor of lions and zebras is therefore a member of Laurasiatheria that lived roughly **55–70 million years ago** during the Paleocene/Eocene.  
It was likely a small, insectivorous or omnivorous mammal that gave rise to the lineages that eventually split into the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla.  

So, the common ancestor of a lion and a zebra is a small, early Laurasiatherian mammal that existed about 60 million years ago.
